name: Trial
label: Equal Vision
lede: Greg Bennick juggled for a living and sang in a Seattle straight edge band that made one album, broke up the next year, then played more shows dead than alive.

eras.title: A juggler takes the mic
eras.text: Seattle was a grunge town. Trial played political straight edge hardcore in it, with Bennick writing about facing suffering instead of hiding from it.

years.h: Seattle gets a political straight edge band with a juggler out front
years.p: Greg Bennick and guitarist Timm McIntosh start Trial. Bennick had taken up juggling at 13 after landing in the wrong school minicourse; he'd signed up for coin collecting.
years.xp:
Bennick's way into hardcore was a friend's cassettes of New York radio shows, which he first thought were terrible. His first show was [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] in 1987, where he met Bob Mould and Grant Hart at a water fountain. For a [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] show a month later, his mother forged him a birth certificate.

He never gave up the coins: Bennick is a numismatist who specializes in error coins and sits on the board of CONECA.

years.h: CrimethInc. puts out Through the Darkest Days
years.p: A mysterious figure called Brian D. approached Trial about a record in 1995. Bennick told Razorcake that CrimethInc. was more a concept than an organization back then.
years.xp: Bennick told Punknews he watched CrimethInc.'s zine grow from one guy in an apartment. He also told Razorcake that band members and roadies were once arrested in Ohio on tour for shoplifting food.

years.h: Foundation comes out on a 7" that plays at 33 RPM
years.p: Trial's second release is also pressed as a CD EP. A compilation LP later pairs it with Through the Darkest Days.

years.h: Bennick's forehead meets McIntosh's headstock in Cleveland
years.p: Mid-set in 1997, Greg Bennick's forehead hit Timm McIntosh's guitar headstock at, as he told Punknews, about a trillion miles per hour. He bled badly.
years.xp: Another road story Bennick told Punknews: his Orthodox Jewish cousin came to her first hardcore show when Trial played Philadelphia. While he was showing her the van, a member of another band on the bill, who had offended [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]], dove inside and locked the doors. Floorpunch members in varsity jackets pounded on the windows until the man slipped away into the night.

eras.title: Months staring at walls
eras.text: Three members quit while Trial wrote its only album, and Bennick and McIntosh finished it with borrowed help. Equal Vision released it in 1999, and a year later the band was over.

years.h: Alexei Rodriguez learns an album in three days
years.p: Three original members quit while Are These Our Lives? was being written. Bassist Brian Redman joined, and drummer Alexei Rodriguez, borrowed from Catharsis, tracked the record in a day and a half.
years.xp:
Bennick told Punknews that the three who left "gave up on the writing process" and that he and McIntosh "crafted it all together."

Rodriguez had three days to learn the album before the studio.

q: Still totally happy with it musically and lyrically.
years.h: Are These Our Lives? goes out without its lyrics
years.p: Greg Bennick spent months on the words for Trial's only full-length, but Equal Vision's first pressing ran without them in the insert.
years.xp:
Bennick told Punknews he'd spent months staring at walls, thinking of words. "That label started releasing copies of the record without lyrics in the insert," he said, and he thought Equal Vision was more excited about radio than the record's message. The one thing he'd change is a phrase in One Step Away.

Trial now treats Panic Records' reissues, with full lyrics and new liner notes, as the authorized versions, and Bennick says Equal Vision isn't authorized to reissue it.

years.big: "A dysfunctional relationship on the verge of explosion."
q: Trial broke up because we, at the time, were a dysfunctional relationship on the verge of explosion.
years.h: Trial split a year after the album
years.p: Bennick's description of the band at the end. He told Punknews the label's handling of Are These Our Lives? was part of it too.
years.xp:
Bennick told Razorcake: "We were fighting over the stupidest things, unable to see eye to eye on the important things, and eventually we pushed one another too far and it fell apart."

To Punknews he said the members "each saw the future of the band differently."

eras.title: A post-mortem existence
eras.text: Bennick turned his fixation on mortality into a documentary while Trial came back a few shows at a time. In 2009, weeks after the band's summer run, bassist Brian Redman was killed.

years.h: Bennick co-produces the documentary Flight from Death
years.p: Made with Patrick Shen and narrated by Gabriel Byrne, the film asks how the fear of death drives human violence. It won audience choice for best documentary at the Beverly Hills Film Festival.

years.cap: Greg Bennick at Trial's 2005 reunion show
years.h: Trial get back together for exactly three shows
years.p: Seattle, London and Budapest, in the fall of 2005. A compilation pairing Through the Darkest Days and Foundation comes out the same year.

years.h: Trial play the Burning Fight book release in Chicago
years.p: Brian Peterson's book on '90s hardcore gets a release show with Trial on the bill.

years.h: Trial top the Fluff Fest bill in the Czech Republic
years.p: Trial headline Fluff Fest on July 25, 2009, then play Antifest in Stockholm in August.

years.src: Exclaim! · DIY Conspiracy · Wikipedia: Trial (Seattle band)
years.h: Brian Redman dies in a scooter crash in Tacoma
years.p: Redman, who played on Are These Our Lives? and later in 3 Inches of Blood, was 31, Exclaim! reported.
years.xp:
Exclaim!, citing police, reported that he was thrown from the scooter after apparently striking a curb. Trial's statement called him one of the most sincere, sarcastic, witty, intelligent, talented guys.

Greg Bennick told DIY Conspiracy a few weeks later that hundreds of people had written to him, and that the band was on hold.

eras.title: More shows than the first time
eras.text: After two quiet years Trial returned with European tours and North American runs, which Bennick called celebrations in Redman's memory, not reunions. The last show was in 2018.

years.h: Trial return without Redman, starting with Rainfest in Seattle
years.p: After two years off, Trial play Rainfest, Chicago's The Rumble, East Coast Tsunami Fest, a surprise New York show and Sound and Fury in Santa Barbara.

years.cap: Greg Bennick onstage with Trial, February 2012
years.h: Europe gets thirty Trial shows, more than the '90s ever did
years.p: Greg Bennick told Razorcake the shows after 2009 were celebrations honoring Brian Redman, not reunions.
years.xp: Bennick described a European tour of 29 shows in 30 days to Razorcake, with crowds from 40 people in Munich to 450 in St. Petersburg.

q: Given that we tour more now than ever, I have to wonder what that means?
years.h: Twelve years after splitting, Trial play 15 North American shows
years.p: Jason Shrout drums on the West Coast. Bennick is also singing in [[Between Earth & Sky|eb394966-a942-4480-a896-9ecd2fd2847e]].
years.xp: Bennick told Punknews that in the last year Trial had "toured more than we did when we were together in the 90s."

years.h: Trial go back to Europe with By the Grace of God
years.p: Trial tour Europe alongside Louisville's [[By the Grace of God|42a5a24f-7fa9-4790-879d-fe5fb3d91f9f]], according to Discogs.

years.h: Trial's last show is a New Age Records birthday party
years.p: They play the label's 30th anniversary at the Garden Amphitheater in Garden Grove, California, with [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and [[Mouthpiece|e4a55353-84ff-4460-9d5a-1666fbe104f4]]. Discogs lists it as their final performance.

years.h: Bennick's Bystander asks Where Did We Go Wrong?
years.p: His post-Trial straight edge band releases the EP, which No Echo featured.
